do_more: Focus explicitly on classic book titles paired with specific section themes (e.g., Book Name · Specific Topic · Reading X)
Use straightforward, academic, and curiosity-driven subject matter directly from public-domain texts rather than modern-style clickbait questions
Maintain a clear episodic structure (e.g., numbered 'Readings') which signals a binge-able series to the viewer
Keep titles descriptive of the actual psychological phenomenon or behavioral observation being analyzed in the text
avoid: Avoid modern pop-psychology listicle hooks and generic self-help questions (e.g., 'Why you buy things you don't need')
Avoid using emojis in the video titles and descriptions
Avoid over-dramatized historical or biographical framing that strays from the core psychological text
title_style: Winning titles clearly state the source book and specific reading topic in a structured format, whereas losing titles rely on modern internet-style hooks and emojis.
next_tests: Test a brand new classic book series using the exact winning format: '[Book Title] · [Specific Concept] · Reading 1'
A/B test a well-performing book title using a straightforward descriptive title versus a modern curiosity-gap hook to verify platform preference
best_title: The Expression of the Emotions in Man and Animals · Watching expression · Reading 5
